## Problem statement

SorraAgents is the canonical installer for pi agent guidance: its scripts/install_pi.sh symlinks the global guidance (AGENTS_GLOBAL.md -> ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md, plus skills and prompts) into every project. The global AGENTS.md already contains the full agent workflow (work-item lifecycle, implement/build-test-commit order, push policy, triage policy).

ContextHub's 'wl init' (src/commands/init.ts) currently has overlapping responsibilities: it prompts for a workflow choice (promptWorkflowChoice: N / B / M, where M is 'Manage custom workflow by editing AGENTS.md directly') and, via ensureWorkflowTemplateInstalled / insertWorkflowLoaderIntoAgents, can inline WORKFLOW content into the project's AGENTS.md. When the SorraAgents global install is present this creates two sources of truth for agent workflow guidance and can conflict with the canonical global file.

## User story

As a developer running wl init on a machine with the SorraAgents install, I want wl init to delegate agent-guidance/workflow setup to the SorraAgents install so the global guidance is the single source of truth and the project AGENTS.md only carries project-specific content.

## Desired change

- When the SorraAgents global install is detected (i.e. ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md resolves to a SorraAgents AGENTS_GLOBAL.md symlink), wl init should NOT inline workflow content into the project AGENTS.md. Instead it should emit/keep the canonical reference structure used by SorraAgents projects:
  - '## Global agent guidance' section referencing ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md
  - '## Project-specific guidance' section for local rules
- wl init should either invoke the SorraAgents install (scripts/install_pi.sh) or clearly document that the SorraAgents install is the canonical mechanism, rather than duplicating guidance.
- The existing pointer-line behavior from 'wl init: prefer global AGENTS.md pointer' (WL-0MLD6N0GW12MNKK0) must be preserved and aligned with the canonical structure above.
- Standalone Worklog users without the SorraAgents install keep the current workflow options (N/B/M) unchanged.

## Success criteria

1. With the SorraAgents global install present, running wl init in a fresh project does not inline WORKFLOW content into AGENTS.md; the file carries the canonical global-reference structure only.
2. wl init output/help documents the SorraAgents install as the canonical global-guidance mechanism (delegation), with no duplicated workflow content.
3. Without the SorraAgents install, existing wl init workflow behavior (N/B/M) is unchanged and existing tests pass.
4. Tests cover both environments (with and without the global SorraAgents symlink).
5. Full ContextHub test suite passes.

## Related work

- ContextHub: 'wl init: prefer global AGENTS.md pointer' (WL-0MLD6N0GW12MNKK0, completed) established the pointer-line behavior this item extends.
- SorraAgents: 'AGENTS.md installer: emit single reference line for new projects' is the complementary installer-side item; the AGENTS.md split (AGENTS_GLOBAL.md canonical source + symlink install) landed in SA-0MSIUUYRD002GC8W.
data.title: Align wl init with SorraAgents install: delegate agent-guidance/workflow setup instead of duplicating

# Feature Request: --fields field-selection for wl list / wl search

## Problem statement

wl list and wl search return full work-item records (or compact snippets for search), with no way to request only the fields a caller needs. Full-record dumps are the root cause of token waste documented in SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ (SorraAgents): bare wl list --json = 5.3 MB / 1,861 records; wl list --status completed = 4.9 MB; scripts (ship gates, triage, code-review) download tens-to-hundreds of KB of fields they never read (e.g. full descriptions) when they only need id, title, status, stage, priority.

## User stories

- As a release-gate script, I want wl list --stage in_review --fields id,title,status,stage,needsProducerReview --json so I stop downloading 4.9 MB of descriptions I discard.
- As an agent running /skill:audit, I want a compact project-status query (fields id,title,status,stage,priority) so the worklog overview stays in the low-KB range.
- As a triage helper, I want wl list --priority critical --tags test-failure --fields id,title,description --json so my match heuristics get exactly the fields they need.

## Expected behaviour

- New option on wl list and wl search: --fields comma-separated (e.g. id,title,status,stage,priority).
- Output objects contain ONLY the requested fields (plus id always, for usability); unknown field names are rejected with a clear error listing valid fields.
- wl list and wl search share the same field vocabulary: id, title, description, status, stage, priority, issueType, assignee, tags, createdAt, updatedAt, parentId, needsProducerReview, sortIndex.
- --json output shape unchanged (same keys; omitted fields absent). Human output uses the same projection for concise display.
- -f as shorthand is acceptable; must not clash with existing flags (-F/--format already taken).

## Acceptance criteria

1. wl list --fields id,title --json returns objects with only id/title; verified for filters and bare queries.
2. wl search term --fields id,title,status --json returns compact objects with only those fields.
3. Invalid field names produce a non-zero exit and a clear error listing valid fields.
4. Output size reduction verified: wl list --stage in_review --fields id,title --json is smaller than the full-record equivalent (target: >=90% reduction for the completed-status case cited above).
5. Existing output without --fields is unchanged (backward compatible); full test suite passes.

## Plan

### Child Work Items (dependency-ordered)

1. **WL-0MT5L3BGA001MKOP** - Create pickFields() projection helper module
2. **WL-0MT5L4MGL000Z43Y** - Write unit tests for pickFields projection helper (depends on 1)
3. **WL-0MT5L55AQ002WTGQ** - Add --fields option to wl list (depends on 1, 2)
4. **WL-0MT5L6G88006N4WD** - Add --fields option to wl search (depends on 1, 2)
5. **WL-0MT5L6TLQ004NDLK** - Integration test: end-to-end --fields flag verification (depends on 3, 4)

### Implementation Approach

1. Create packages/shared/src/fields.ts with pickFields(item, fields?) helper
2. Add fields?: string to ListOptions and SearchOptions in cli-types.ts
3. Apply pickFields projection in list.ts before JSON output
4. Apply pickFields projection in search.ts before JSON output
5. Write unit tests and integration tests

### Review Stages Summary

1. Requirements & AC alignment: All 5 ACs map to user stories and expected behaviour. No gaps or contradictions.
2. Completeness: Description has all required sections. Key files are valid.
3. Sequencing & dependencies: Test items before implementation items. Dependencies properly set.
4. Scope sizing: Small effort, Low risk - appropriate for scope.
5. Acceptance & testability: All ACs are testable with clear pass/fail criteria.
6. Polish & handoff: Plan is copy-pasteable and actionable.

## Plan Changelog

- 2026-08-23T09:09Z - Plan created with 5 child work items. Pre-check: Small effort, Low risk. All review stages passed.

## Appendix

- Q: Should --fields support nested field access (e.g. auditResult.readyToClose)? Answer (plan agent): No. The work item scope is flat field selection only. Nested access can be added later if needed. Final: not in scope.
- Q: Should -f shorthand be supported? Answer (plan agent): Yes, but -f is not taken in either list or search. Final: -f can be added as shorthand.
data.title: Add --fields option to wl list and wl search for field-selective output

# Intake Brief: Sync — Regression Guard

## Problem Statement

When `wl sync` merges remote state that is newer than local, it can silently import regressions: fields the local store had set to non-default values (e.g. `effort: 'Small'`, `status: completed`) get overwritten with defaults by a stale/divergent second store, as observed Aug 6–10, 2026 on the llm worklog ref.

## Users

- **Primary**: Operators of multi-store worklog setups — anyone running more than one `wl sync` instance against the same remote.
- **Secondary**: Producers/reviewers whose audit results (status/stage transitions) are silently reverted by stale syncs.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. During merge, for each incoming remote item with a newer `updatedAt` than local, detect regressions where a field moves from a non-default value to its default on the fields that participate in the merge: `status`/`stage` (non-default → default, e.g. `completed/in_review` → `open/idea`), `priority` (non-default → default), and `assignee` (set → unset).

   **`effort`/`risk` (producer resolution, 2026-08-23): stay PERMANENTLY EXCLUDED from the merge field lists** — ping-pong prevention by construction. A remote `effort: ''` / `risk: ''` never enters the merge; local non-default values are always kept. The guard additionally REPORTS any attempted effort/risk regression (remote non-empty → default) as a protected conflict (local kept, nothing imported) for observability, but no override path is needed for these two fields since they cannot be imported through the merge.
2. On detecting a regression, `wl sync` refuses to import that item's regressed fields: reports the conflict (item id, field, old local value, new remote default value) and keeps the local value. An explicit override flag (`--accept-regressions` or equivalent) allows the operator to accept the regression.
3. Genuine concurrent edits (both stores changed different non-default fields, or both changed the same field to different non-default values) still merge and re-timestamp exactly as today — this guard must NOT change legitimate conflict resolution.
4. The regression guard applies only to the `import()`/merge path used by `wl sync` — it does NOT affect explicit user `wl update` commands, which remain authoritative.
5. Unit tests cover: (a) newer remote with `effort: ''` against local `effort: 'Small'` → local kept (exclusion by construction), conflict REPORTED as protected, remote value NOT imported; (b) newer remote with `status: open` against local `completed` → refused, local kept, conflict reported; (c) both sides non-default differing → normal merge + re-timestamp (no regression path — guard must NOT alter legitimate conflict resolution); (d) override flag accepts the regression for merge-participating fields only; (e) `--dry-run` reports the same refusals.
6. Manual verification: sync against the known commit `5fc880a` (effort/risk cleared) → regressions refused and reported; sync against `54b1375` (restored values) → no regression flags.

## Constraints

- Must not change behavior for legitimate concurrent edits — the guard is regression-only, not conflict-resolution.
- Must be deterministic: dry-run and normal sync report the same refusals.
- Does NOT prevent a second store from pushing — it prevents the primary store from absorbing regressive state.
- Complements the identity gate (WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB) — the identity gate catches the writer; this guard catches the damage even if the writer's identity is unknown.

## Existing State

The merge functions (`mergeSameTimestampItems`, `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` in `src/sync.ts`) already implement a non-default-preference heuristic: when one side has a non-default value and the other has a default, the non-default is preserved. The `isDefaultValue` helper in `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` classifies empty strings, `undefined`, and empty arrays as defaults.

The merge field arrays include `status`, `stage`, `priority`, and `assignee` — these fields **already** keep the local non-default value when the remote sends a default (via the `!localIsDefault && remoteIsDefault` branch). They do **not** produce an explicit regression report — the local value is silently kept.

The merge field arrays do **not** include `effort` or `risk` — these fields are never merged at all; the local value is always preserved regardless of the remote.

**Contradiction — RESOLVED (producer decision, 2026-08-23)**: The 13-field merge list currently excludes `effort`/`risk` (code-confirmed), yet the original ACs listed them as regression targets. Producer directive: *"The goal is to prevent ping-pong — do what you need to."* Resolution: **Reading A** — `effort`/`risk` remain excluded from the merge lists; adding them to the merge would re-introduce the ping-pong (the DB re-timestamp amplifier in `hasWorkItemChanged` already tracks these fields, so a single unguarded import becomes the newest record and propagates). The guard therefore targets the merge-participating fields (`status`/`stage`/`priority`/`assignee`), and `effort`/`risk` regressions are reported as protected (local kept). Effort/risk merge-participation is a non-goal.

## Desired Change

Add a regression detection layer on top of the merge path that:
- Identifies fields regressing from non-default → default in newer remote state, for the merge-participating fields: `status`/`stage`/`priority`/`assignee`
- Reports conflicts with details (item id, field, old value, new value)
- Refuses to import regressed fields (keeping local) unless overridden (`--accept-regressions`, merge-participating fields only)
- Preserves all existing merge behavior for non-regression cases
- Reports (without importing) attempted `effort`/`risk` regressions as protected — these fields remain excluded from the merge lists (non-goal: adding them back)

## Risks & Assumptions

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Regression detection logic breaks existing merge behavior | High | Unit tests must verify non-regression cases still merge correctly (AC3) |
| Scope creep: "regression" definition might be too broad (e.g., should a valid transition like `in_progress → open` count as regression?) | Medium | Strict definition: only non-default → default transitions count |
| Override flag (`--accept-regressions`) could be misused, allowing silent data loss | Medium | Require explicit flag; report what was accepted in output |
| **DECIDED**: effort/risk must NOT be added to the merge list | — | Producer resolution 2026-08-23: adding them re-introduces ping-pong (DB re-timestamp amplifier `hasWorkItemChanged` tracks these fields; one unguarded import becomes the newest record) |
| `isDefaultValue` may not correctly identify defaults for all fields (e.g., custom stages) | Low | Only built-in defaults (`open`, `idea`, `medium`, empty strings) are guarded; custom stages fall through to normal merge |
| **Scope-creep risk**: The guard could be extended to "merge strategies" or general conflict-policy work — those are separate concerns. | Medium | Record as future work items; do not implement here |

**Assumptions**:
- The `isDefaultValue` function correctly classifies all default values for the fields in question
- Regression detection can be cleanly layered on top of existing merge logic without restructuring
- The operator will accept a new CLI flag for override

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/sync.ts` — `mergeSameTimestampItems`, `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`: add regression detection alongside the existing merge logic (field lists UNCHANGED for `effort`/`risk` — exclusion is the ping-pong prevention)
- `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` — `isDefaultValue`: may need no changes (already classifies empties as defaults)
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — CLI flag for `--accept-regressions`, conflict reporting in output
- `tests/sync-regression-guard.test.ts` — new test file for regression detection scenarios

## Related Work

| ID | Title | Relationship |
|----|-------|-------------|
| WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB | Sync: identity gate — refuse merge of foreign/empty-author commits | Related: same root cause incident (Aug 2026 llm worklog pollution); identity gate catches the writer, regression guard catches the damage |
| WL-0MSORD6HC005QVZX | Sync: do not change updatedAt on whitespace-only changes | Completed; orthogonal concern |
| WL-0MKVZ510K1XHJ7B3 | Sync & data integrity | Completed; foundational sync merge logic |
| WL-0MSUEOAQO0081TJH | Wire identity gate into wl sync + config flag + sync-point persistence | Completed; identity gate now wired into sync |

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

- **Q (auto-resolved by code inspection)**: The description says "the 13-field merge list currently excludes effort/risk" — the code confirms `effort` and `risk` are NOT in the merge field arrays. Does this mean: (a) the ACs about effort/risk are stale and should be removed, or (b) the description is outdated and effort/risk regressions need explicit detection and reporting? → **Answer (producer, 2026-08-23): "The goal is to prevent ping-pong — do what you need to." Interpreted as Reading A: effort/risk stay excluded from the merge lists (prevention by construction); the guard targets merge-participating fields (status/stage/priority/assignee) and reports protected effort/risk conflict attempts without importing them. Adding effort/risk to the merge is a non-goal.** Source: interactive reply, this intake session (2026-08-23).
- **Q**: What is the exact override flag name? The ACs mention `--accept-regressions` or equivalent. → **Flagged for producer confirmation.**
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MS8XLS0Z00759QI** – Pi TUI tools.ts: smart selection (helper copy + fetch merge + apply) (completed)
- **WL-0MSVRMAWM007QNR5** – Downtime worker: parseLlamaStatus rejects numeric slot_id — every poll fail-closes to busy, zero dispatches (completed)
- **WL-0MSHWHFAK005WKDB** – [test-failure] defaultSettings has default browseItemCount of 10 — failing test (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: ac3, accept, acceptance, accepted, accepts (+231 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: ac3, accept, acceptance, accepted, accepts (+204 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: accept, accepts, add, adding, affect (+191 more)
data.title: Sync: regression guard — refuse import of default-value regressions from newer remote state

# Allow bounded concurrent downtime dispatches during cheap mode (use both local slots)

## Problem statement

Proxy usage analysis of the 04:00-06:00 cheap-mode window (2026-08-22 report, `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`) shows the local Qwen3 model busy only ~25-38% of the window. Root cause is structural, not demand: the downtime worker dispatches strictly **single-flight** (one work item at a time, WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY), each dispatched session consumes exactly **one** local slot, and cheap mode provides **two** slots. The second cheap slot is essentially never used, and the per-item tail (agent tool-execution gaps between generation bursts, 10s-5min each) is pure idle that nothing else can fill.

24 herdr `audit-WL-*` sessions ran nearly sequentially: short generation bursts (3-10s) separated by long tool-execution gaps. Inter-run scheduler dead time (60s idle threshold + 10s poll + spawn) added another ~70s per dispatch cycle.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — pays for remote fallback tokens; wants maximum value from the always-on local iGPU during cheap hours (01:00-10:00).
- **Herdr downtime users** — want more audits/work items completed per night.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. During cheap mode, the downtime worker MAY dispatch a second work item to fill an otherwise-idle second local slot, subject to a bounded concurrency cap (start with 2 concurrent dispatches).
2. Dispatch of the second item respects the same idle-gate contract (requires `requiredFreeSlots` free slots observed for the idle-threshold duration) — it must NOT queue or dispatch into a busy slot.
3. The concurrency cap is configurable via downtime settings (default 1 = current behavior, so fast/operator-interactive mode is unchanged unless explicitly enabled).
4. Fast mode (3 slots) and operator-interactive sessions keep priority: downtime never displaces an active operator session slot; only genuinely free slots are used.
5. Tests: bounded-concurrency dispatch logic (cap honored, second dispatch only fires when ≥1 slot free for N polls), no regression to existing single-flight claim safety (WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY).
6. Measured outcome: nightly cheap-window busy % for the local model increases vs. baseline (target ≥ 2x the current ~25-38%).

## Notes

- Coupling: dispatched audits run `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1`, so ONE audit uses at most 1 slot (parent then child serially). Two concurrent audits therefore use at most 2 slots = exactly cheap mode's capacity (WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS). Raising fan-out (see the AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM item) changes this budget and must be coordinated — total in-flight local streams must not exceed the cheap pool.
- Related: WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (same-slot idle tracking), WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (audit fan-out bound), WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY (single-flight dispatch), WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2 (referenced in code comments, not found in worklog — verify against per-slot idle tracker).
- The 04:00-06:00 evidence (24 sessions, 252 local streams, 48% idle stream-level) is in `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` and the analysis session log.
data.title: Allow bounded concurrent downtime dispatches (use both cheap-mode slots)

# Intake Brief: Fair round-robin work scheduling with priority override (WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V)

## Problem Statement
The `dispatchFromCoordination` leader path in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` selects from the shared coordination file (`downtime-coordination.json`) by iterating entries in file order within each tier. With multiple projects contributing (ContextHub, SorraAgents, AI_Hell, Tableau-Card-Engine), this allows the same project to monopolise consecutive dispatch slots. We need globally-fair distribution with an exception for critical-priority items.

## Users

- **Agent — Automated downtime worker (primary):** As a downtime worker I want dispatches to fairly represent all contributing projects, so that no single project starves others of agent attention.
- **Developer / Project owner:** As a developer with work in an unserved project, I want the scheduler to eventually assign my project's candidate even when another project has more frequent offers, so that my backlog makes progress.

### User Stories
- As the downtime dispatcher leader, when entries exist from multiple projects at the same tier, I select the project whose last dispatch (in any tier) is oldest (round-robin), so that projects get a fair share of slots.
- As a project owner with a `critical`-priority offer on file, my next dispatch should bypass round-robin and run immediately (still at its stage-appropriate skill), so that urgent work is not delayed by fairness.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `dispatchFromCoordination` selects across the shared coordination entries in **global cross-project round-robin** order: among equally-eligible (tier-matched, non-critical) entries, the project whose `worklogRoot` was least-recently dispatched (with persistence across leader restarts / cycles) is chosen first. New / unknown roots sort first (never penalised). A single persistent cursor/state per worklog root (e.g. in a JSON file alongside the coordination file) drives the ordering; concurrent leaders do not corrupt the cursor (fail-open).
- [ ] When **any** entry on file is a `critical`-priority open item at a dispatchable stage (`idea` / `intake_complete` / `plan_complete` within caps; stage-appropriate skill), the leader dispatches that critical entry **immediately** ahead of all non-critical entries, regardless of round-robin position. Within the critical subset, selection remains deterministic (existing priority/sortIndex tie-break — one item per project, so round-robin is not needed inside critical).
- [ ] The critical override is **global** (evaluated before any tier loop): a critical in `plan_complete` outranks a non-critical `audit`, and a critical `idea` outranks a non-critical `implement`, matching the intent "jump to the front of the queue". The existing freeze (audit/implement skipped while frozen) and caps (`risk <= Medium && effort <= Medium` for `plan_complete`, including critical) are retained.
- [ ] After a successful dispatch (or a `spawn-failed`/`marker-write-failed` claim that still consumes the entry), the round-robin cursor/state advances to mark that project's `worklogRoot` as most-recently served, so the next dispatch in **any** tier starts from the following project.
- [ ] Existing `downtime-worker` and `coordination` tests still pass, plus new tests prove: (a) with two non-critical entries from different projects at the same tier, consecutive dispatches alternate projects; (b) a newly-arrived critical from project B is dispatched next even though round-robin would choose project A; (c) cursor persists across a simulated leader restart.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints
- Must build on the existing coordination machinery (`packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` lock + atomic write, `machine-coordination.ts` single machine dir) — no new daemon or external dependency.
- Fail-open on missing/corrupt round-robin state (behaves as if no history — original file order), never throws or starves dispatch.
- No behaviour change to `wl next` / single-project flows; this is strictly the multi-project leader path (`coordinationDir` present).
- Preserve dispatched-marker exclusion and CAS claim ordering already in `dispatchFromCoordination`.
- Each project currently registers at most one offer per cycle, so per-project multiplicity can be treated as one entry per root — design should not break if that grows, but need not optimise for many-per-root.

## Existing State
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchFromCoordination` groups fetched entries by tier (`audit` → `critical` → `implement` → `plan` → `intake`) and iterates each group in file order (`entries` array order). No cross-project fairness: repeated offers from the same root can win every slot when they re-queue quickly.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin.ts` provides a per-tier persistent cursor for the *legacy* `selectWithRotation` path (unused in coordination mode); the new requirement is **global, cross-tier** round-robin across `worklogRoot`s.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` manages `downtime-coordination.json` with atomic tmp+rename and an `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` lock (`tryAcquireCoordLock` / `withCoordLock`), and already carries `worklogRoot` per entry; `machine-coordination.ts` makes the file machine-wide.
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination-cross-root.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin.test.ts`.
- Contributing projects: ContextHub, SorraAgents, AI_Hell, Tableau-Card-Engine (each instance writes one entry via `runCoordinationCheckIn`).

## Desired Change
- Introduce a **global per-project round-robin** ordering for `dispatchFromCoordination`: track last-dispatched `worklogRoot` (persistent JSON alongside the coordination file, e.g. `downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`), sort same-tier eligible candidates by "least-recently-served first" before dispatch, and advance the cursor on each consumed entry.
- Promote the **critical override** to a global pre-tier check: re-fetch → if any dispatchable critical exists, dispatch the first critical immediately (respecting freeze/caps), before the tier-ordered round-robin loop.
- Add/extend tests to cover alternating-project fairness, critical jump-ahead, and cursor durability; update `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and relevant code comments.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Needs updated `dispatchFromCoordination` + new helpers for global round-robin ordering / cursor advance
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — May gain small helpers or remain unchanged (new state file is separate)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin.ts` — May be reused/extended or a new `downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` added for worklogRoot-keyed persistence
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — Reference for machine-dir resolution used by the new state file
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — Needs new fair-scheduling test cases
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — Needs updated dispatch ordering description (fair scheduling + critical override)

## Related Work
- Parent area: `WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL` (Refactor Downtime Dispatcher: leader election + shared coordination file), `WL-0MTF0KLO10043YAN` (Single machine-wide leader), `WL-0MTII45EP002DWK6` (Cross-directory tier dispatch)
- Preceding round-robin work: `WL-0MSSRED76008LGB6` + `downtime-round-robin.ts` / `downtime-round-robin.test.ts` (per-tier cursor, now superseded by global root-level rotation)
- Tier / dispatch reference: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:COORDINATION_TIER_ORDER`, `classifyItemForDispatch`, `COORDINATION_FILE` / `readCoordinationFile` in `coordination.ts`
- Follow-up opportunity: if per-root multiplicity grows beyond one, consider weighted or deficit round-robin (record as a linked work item, not in scope)

## Risks & Assumptions
- **Risk:** Cursor file races between leaders → Mitigation: reuse the existing `withCoordLock` / tmp+rename pattern; fail-open when lock is contended.
- **Risk:** New critical items arriving between fetch and dispatch could be missed → Mitigation: critical check happens on the same single fetch pass; subsequent arrivals wait one cycle (acceptable at 30-min check-in cadence).
- **Risk:** Stale-entry pruning removes a root before its round-robin turn → Mitigation: pruned roots drop from ordering automatically; no ghost cursor entries block others.
- **Risk:** Scope creep (e.g. per-entry priority weighting beyond critical) → Mitigation: explicitly out of scope; non-critical priorities are treated as equally round-robined (per operator: one item per project).
- **Assumption:** At most one entry per `worklogRoot` per cycle — holds today; ordering by `worklogRoot` last-served is equivalent to ordering by entry last-served.
- **Assumption:** "Jump to the front" means dispatch before any non-critical regardless of tier, not just within the same tier — confirmed with operator (clarification round: globally, dispatch immediately).
- **Assumption:** Persistence should survive leader restarts and machine reboot → file on disk in the machine coordination dir, not in-memory only.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "What constitutes a 'project' for fair scheduling?" — Answer (user): "The multi-project downtime scheduling recently implemented — leader election with one work item per project via the herdr extension. Currently ContextHub, ../SorraAgents, ../AI_Hell, ../Tableau-Card-Engine." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Is this about `wl next` or the coordination dispatch?" — Answer (user): "The multi-project case — nothing to do with `wl next`." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "When a project has a critical item, does it jump the queue?" — Answer (user): "yes" (affirmative — critical from any project jumps ahead). Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Do non-critical priorities (high/medium/low) matter within round-robin?" — Answer (user): "I believe each project only registers a single work item so this is not important." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Round-robin scope — per-tier or globally?" — Answer (user): "globally" Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Critical override granularity — immediate dispatch or just cursor bump?" — Answer (user): "dispatch immediately" Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Should the cursor persist across cycles/restarts?" — Answer (user): "persistent" Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.

# Interview Replay Feature

**Headline:** Add a `wl <id> interview` CLI command that provides an interactive walkthrough of outstanding interview questions on a work item, capturing responses and clearing the producer review flag.

## Problem Statement

When a work item has interview questions that need answers, the questions are recorded in the work item description but are difficult for a producer to locate and respond to later. There is no structured mechanism to walk through outstanding questions systematically.

## Users

- **Producers** who review and approve work items — need an efficient way to answer outstanding interview questions without manually searching through the work item description.

**User Story:** "As a producer reviewing a work item, I want the system to walk me through each outstanding interview question so I can answer them quickly without hunting through the description."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new CLI command `wl <id> interview` is available and interactive.
2. The command displays a brief summary of the work item (title, current status, and context).
3. The command identifies and asks each outstanding question from the work item's interview questions (clarifying questions & answers section in the description).
4. The command waits for a response to each question before proceeding to the next.
5. All answers are recorded back into the work item description in the clarifying questions section.
6. After all questions are answered, `needsProducerReview` is set to `false`.
7. The command handles edge cases gracefully: no questions present (exit cleanly), and interrupted sessions can be resumed.

## Constraints

- The command must work in a terminal with interactive input (readline/stdin).
- Answers must be persisted to the work item's description in the existing clarifying questions format.
- The command should handle edge cases: no questions present, partial answers already recorded.

## Existing State

- Interview questions are embedded in the work item description under a "Clarifying questions & answers" section.
- The `needsProducerReview` flag exists as a database column and CLI filter.
- No existing command walks through questions interactively.

## Desired Change

Add a new `interview` subcommand that provides an interactive walkthrough of outstanding questions, capturing responses and updating the work item state.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/interview.ts` — New command implementation
- `src/commands/helpers.ts` — May need helper for extracting questions from description
- `src/database.ts` — For updating the work item description and needsProducerReview flag
- `src/cli-types.ts` — CLI type definitions for the new command

## Related Work

- **WL-0MLGVVMR70IC1S8F**: Run DB migration: add needsProducerReview column — establishes the flag that this command will set to false.
- **WL-0MSLPM5ZB003TADT**: Sort in_review items — related to producer workflow.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSJ4BT4Z002HH9B** – Fully remove deprecated icons.ts from all projects that use it (src + herdr) (completed)
- **WL-0MKZ2GZBK1JS1IZF** – Work Items tree shows completed items after filters (completed)
- **WL-0MQDR5JBV0054CBY** – End-to-end test for detail view shortcut result handling (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `package/packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mslpm5zb003tadt, acceptance, add, additional, already (+116 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mslpm5zb003tadt, acceptance, add, additional, already (+116 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: add, additional, already, answer, asks (+95 more)

## Clarifying Questions & Answers

No clarifying questions were asked. The existing work item description was sufficiently detailed to draft a clear brief (problem statement, proposed command name, expected behaviour, and outcomes were all explicit).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption**: Interview questions follow a consistent format in the description that can be parsed programmatically.
- **Assumption**: The clarifying questions format is stable and documented.
- **Risk**: Parsing description text to extract questions may be brittle if formats vary.
- **Risk**: Edge case — what if a question is answered inline but not in the formal section?
- **Risk**: Partial interview — what if the producer is interrupted mid-way through? Need to handle resume.
- **Scope creep**: Additional features like batch answering or exporting questions should be captured as follow-up work items, not in this scope.

# Triage the 18 non-terminal children of v1.0.16-shipped parents

## Class B — genuinely unimplemented (4 items)

No commits, still `intake_complete`. Recommended: re-parent to a new successor epic (e.g. "Herdr hydrator — remaining scope") so the shipped parent WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI can close without sweeping them.

- WL-0MTF5WNZV003JKMJ — Docs: herdr hydrator section
- WL-0MTF5WO1N0088P5P — Worklist: hydrate task + focus-resume
- WL-0MTF5WO2Q008B8US — Hydrator: demote stale in_progress items
- WL-0MTF5WO4Q005YBVH — Hydrator: unit test suite

## Why the parents were blocked

- WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4, WL-0MUD6DDZC007ZSIW, WL-0MU6UL0RJ008IHGT, WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28: blocked by Class A children.
- WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI: blocked by Class B children.

## Root cause / prevention

Parents reached `in_review` (`status: completed`) while their children were still non-terminal. Investigate whether the audit-runner `inherited_pass` bypass (SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0 in SorraAgents) allowed this, and add a guard so a parent cannot advance to `in_review` with non-terminal children (or record an explicit partial-ship decision).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Class A children advanced to `in_review`/`completed` with audits, then closed as shipped; their parents (WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4, WL-0MUD6DDZC007ZSIW, WL-0MU6UL0RJ008IHGT, WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28) transition to `stage: done`.
2. Class B children re-parented to a successor epic and the parent WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI closed, with no non-terminal child swept.
3. Prevention measure implemented or explicitly deferred with a linked work item.
4. `wl doctor` reports no new issues for the affected items.

data.description: Prune and rotate audit_debug JSONL files across worklog stores. ContextHub/.worklog and open_source_llm/.worklog are 13 GB and 11 GB respectively, with individual files up to 1.9 GB last updated 2026-08-01 — nearly 8 weeks stale. These files cause runaway grep scans (e.g. 4.4 GB read, 12+ min, 48% CPU) and bloat every worklog operation. Strategy: implement a cron-based rotation (rotate after 7 days or 50 MB per file), archive older files to cold storage or delete, and add a hygiene check script to .worklog/.gitignore or a pre-commit hook.

data.description: 50 concurrent pi agent sessions are consuming 12.4 GB RSS with ages up to 18+ hours. Multiple sessions appear abandoned: their work (intake, plan) has completed but the sessions remain alive with no child processes. Orphaned audit_runner processes reparented to PID 1 confirm parent sessions have died without cleanup. This contributes to severe CPU oversubscription (load 3× cores). Root cause analysis needed: does the plan/intake skill fail to transition session state, or is there a missing lifecycle hook? Implement a fix so sessions auto-close or mark complete on skill completion.

Create a new skill (proposed name: host-hygiene or perf-hygiene) that automates the manual machine-health analysis performed on 2026-09-27 (which resolved load 44 on 16 cores, CPU pressure 88.8%, a runaway 4.4 GB grep, orphaned audit_runners and stale vite servers).

## Purpose
A repeatable, safe diagnostic-and-remediation skill for hosts running many concurrent pi agent sessions and test suites. It must NEVER act autonomously without explicit producer approval.

## Required workflow (must be encoded in the skill)
1. **Evaluate** — collect performance metrics (load average, /proc/pressure/{cpu,memory,io}, free/swap, process & thread counts, per-command aggregate RSS, runnable count, stale devices) and render a before table with status symbols: low / warning / critical.
2. **Detail** — describe the primary pressures (which processes, which resources, attributable ancestry).
3. **Suggest** — propose concrete actions to relieve pressure (kills, pruning, pacing, session cleanup), each with target PIDs/paths and expected impact.
4. **Await producer input** — STOP. Present findings and wait for explicit approval. Do not kill, delete, or modify anything.
5. **Act on approval** — perform only the explicitly approved subset of actions.
6. **After table** — add an 'after' column to the original table showing current state, with per-metric priorities, and report residual/legitimate load.

## Constraints
- Read-only by default; destructive actions gated behind operator/producer approval.
- Must use wl for any work-item side effects and never edit .worklog data directly.
- Reusable across projects (global skill under skill/), with tests per skill-authoring conventions.
- Reference the analysis in WL-0MUJL0PTS009MC8F (debug-log rotation) and WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS (session close lifecycle) as related root causes.

## Acceptance criteria (draft)
- Skill file exists with the 6-step workflow and an explicit approval gate before any mutation.
- Diagnostic step reproduces the before/after tables (load, pressure, memory, swap, procs, threads, per-command RSS).
- Status symbols (low/warning/critical) defined with thresholds.
- Skill takes no destructive action in steps 1-4; step 5 only operates on an approved list.
- Tests cover threshold classification and the approval-gate refusal path.
- Documented in the skill index / discoverable via /skill invocation.
data.title: Create a machine-hygiene skill that evaluates performance pressure and proposes remediations
